title: Real-time delivery: subscribers see a message on commit, and a machine's runner wakes its idle sessions

story.as_a: session waiting for input on a fleet machine
story.i_want_to: be woken by my machine's runner when a message arrives for me, and Mark's dashboard to see every message as it lands
story.so_that: a message to an idle session no longer waits until someone types

rationale: PRD R11: the coordination-bus design chose store-and-poll and no WebSockets for agents (docs/repo-coordination-bus.md section 5), which misses the idle session; an idle session is woken by its machine's host daemon, which holds a Phoenix Channels subscription and hands the message over through Claude Code's local cross-session delivery, and fleet_dash subscribes to the same stream. The runner already holds one: it joins runner:<runner_id> on LoopctlWeb.RunnerSocket (lib/loopctl_web/runner_socket.ex:48) and receives control -> runner pushes (dispatch, merge; lib/loopctl/api_spec/runner_contract.ex:29-39). That socket authenticates only runner tokens (runner_socket.ex:55-101), so fleet_dash, which holds a user api key, needs a socket of its own. PRD section 9 leaves the wake mechanism to a measurement on Linux and macOS, with delivery at the next turn as the fallback.

acceptance_criteria.description: After a message's transaction commits, Messages broadcasts {:message, summary} on the PubSub topic messages:<tenant_id>, where summary is id, attachment kind and id, attachment_seq, agent_id, author_holder_id, inserted_at and a body preview of at most 512 bytes; a rolled-back send broadcasts nothing.

LoopctlWeb.MessageSocket at /socket/messages authenticates the api key in the x-loopctl-api-key header with Loopctl.Auth.verify_api_key/1, and LoopctlWeb.MessageChannel admits a join of topic messages:tenant only for a key of role :user or above, pushing a message event per summary of that key's tenant; an :agent or :orchestrator key's join is refused with reason unauthorized.

For a committed DM, or a thread message whose story has an assigned_holder_id, whose recipient holder is live (ended_at nil), loopctl pushes inbox_wake {holder_id, session_id, unread} (no body) on runner:<runner_id> of each live runner of the tenant whose joined machine equals the holder's host, only to runners that joined declaring the contract version that adds RunnerInboxWake or later.

On every runner join, and every 300 s while joined, LoopctlWeb.RunnerChannel pushes inbox_wake for each live holder of the tenant whose host equals the runner's machine and whose inbox (Messages.inbox/3) is not empty, so a wake lost to a node restart, a dropped broadcast or a suspended machine is sent again.

The runner (runner/lib/loopctl_runner/control.ex handle_message/4) validates inbox_wake against the contract and hands it to LoopctlRunner.SessionWake, which wakes one holder at most once per 60 s, coalescing every wake inside that window into one.

docs/factory/measurements/idle-session-wake.md records, for Linux (minis) and macOS (mac-mini), whether the runner process can deliver a fixed text into an idle interactive Claude Code session through the local cross-session delivery (a direct write to the session's local socket, then the restricted headless courier of claude-config bin/fleet-nudge.sh) with no approval prompt, whether the recipient can be addressed by its session id, and the delivery latency.

LoopctlRunner.SessionWake uses, per operating system, the first mechanism the measurement shows working, sending only the fixed text 'You have unread loopctl inbox messages. Read them with the inbox tool now.'; where none worked it uses the NextTurn adapter, which delivers nothing, logs the gap once per runner start, and leaves delivery to the session's next tool round.

test_cases.name: broadcast after commit only (DataCase)
steps: Messages.send/4 a message whose body fails the denylist
expected_results: one {:message, summary} with a 512-byte preview and the stored id; nothing for the refused send

test_cases.name: fleet_dash socket: user key joins, agent key refused, other tenant unseen (ChannelCase)
preconditions: user key and agent key in tenant A; user key in tenant B (test/support/channel_case.ex)
steps: connect MessageSocket with each key in x-loopctl-api-key and join messages:tenant
send a message in tenant A
expected_results: tenant A user receives one message push; agent key join {:error, %{reason: "unauthorized"}}; tenant B user receives nothing; a bad key fails connect

test_cases.name: wake routed to the runner on the holder's machine (ChannelCase, runner_channel tests)
preconditions: fixture(:runner) R1 joined with machine "minis" at the new contract version; R2 joined with machine "x1"; R3 on minis joined at the previous version; holder H on host minis holding story S; ended holder E on minis
steps: send a thread message on S
send a DM to E (refused, US-52.25)
expected_results: R1 gets two inbox_wake pushes for H with no body field; R2 and R3 get none; nothing for E or the channel message

test_cases.name: join and periodic reconciliation re-send lost wakes (ChannelCase)
preconditions: holder H on minis with one unacked DM sent while no runner was joined; holder G on minis with an empty inbox
steps: send :reconcile_inbox to the channel process (the 300 s timer's message)
expected_results: one inbox_wake for H on join and one on the tick; none for G

test_cases.name: runner coalesces wakes per holder (runner ExUnit)
preconditions: SessionWake with a recording adapter and an injected clock
steps: deliver 5 inbox_wake for H within 10 s
advance the clock 61 s and deliver one more
expected_results: the adapter is called twice for H; the malformed payload is refused by contract validation and never reaches the adapter

test_cases.name: adapter selection follows the recorded measurement (runner ExUnit)
preconditions: runner config with wake adapters {linux: Courier, macos: NextTurn} as the measurement file records; a fake courier executable that records its argv
expected_results: linux: the courier runs once with the fixed text and H's session id and no other text; macos: nothing runs and one gap log line is written for the runner's life

technical_notes: PubSub: broadcast with Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(Loopctl.PubSub, ...) after Messages.send/4's transaction returns {:ok, ...} (never inside it); the cluster carries it to the node holding each socket, as Runners.dispatch_topic/1 does (lib/loopctl/runners.ex:131, broadcast :699-716).

New socket because none could serve: LiveView's /live socket is browser-session-bound and RunnerSocket admits only runner tokens. Mount /socket/messages in lib/loopctl_web/endpoint.ex beside /runner/socket (:72-75) with websocket connect_info [:x_headers], longpoll false, an explicit drainer (issue #815: every socket's drainer is explicit and fly.toml kill_timeout derives from them, endpoint.ex:56-59).

Runner channel: RunnerChannel subscribes to a per-runner wake topic in handle_info(:after_join) (lib/loopctl_web/runner_channel.ex:209, Presence.track :229) and pushes inbox_wake like merge (:280-289); the runner's machine is the joined RunnerJoin machine field (runner_contract.ex RunnerJoin; runner side join_payload/4 in loopctl-runner lib/loopctl_runner/control.ex:436-470, at runner/ after release 2). Holder host and session_id: holders.host and holders.session_id (US-52.13). Wake routing lookup: live holders of the message's recipient, then Runners.pool/1 (runners.ex:147) entries whose meta machine equals the host.

Contract: add RunnerInboxWake (holder_id, session_id, unread integer >= 1) and the control -> runner event inbox_wake to lib/loopctl/api_spec/runner_contract.ex (event table :29-39, @version :436, event map :4605-4611), bump the minor, re-vendor in runner/; the runner's catch-all handle_message/4 (control.ex:1573) keeps ignoring it on an older runner, so either side may deploy first (R7).

Security: the wake carries no body, so a session that registered a false host (holders.host is session-reported, PRD R4) can at most cause a wake on the wrong machine, which finds no such session; the message itself is read only with the recipient's own credential (US-52.24).

Measurement method: on each OS start an interactive claude session in tmux, let it go idle, then from a process running as the runner's user try (a) a direct write to the session's local delivery socket and (b) the courier flag set at claude-config bin/fleet-nudge.sh:1153-1161 (--tools SendMessage,ListAgents, --strict-mcp-config, --disallowedTools mcp__*, cwd ~/.claude/courier-cwd); a macOS courier started outside the GUI session needs the published credential file (bin/mac-creds-publish.sh, session-message.sh:51-58). Record the claude version, the result and the latency. PRD section 9 open question; the result decides the adapter map in runner config, and the gap, if any, is written in the same file.

Courier adapter: runner/lib/loopctl_runner/session_wake/courier.ex runs the courier with stdin closed (fleet-nudge.sh:1144-1152 explains why) under the runner's existing process-group supervision (loopctl-runner lib/loopctl_runner/process_group.ex), with a 120 s timeout; a failed wake is logged and dropped, because the reconciliation tick (AC-52.27.4) sends it again.
non_goals: The session-side hooks (SessionStart inbox block, tool-round reads) and deleting session-message.sh: US-52.28.
Capacity reports and CI runner registration on the runner socket: release 7 (README names table: host daemon).
Keeping one machine per region running so subscriptions survive Fly suspend: release 10 (PRD R9); until then the reconciliation tick covers a dropped socket.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.27.4: a runner cut off from loopctl misses wakes; when it rejoins, the join pushes a wake for every holder on its machine with unread messages, and the messages themselves were stored before any push (AC-52.27.1).
failure_modes.state: AC-52.27.1 and AC-52.27.3: PubSub, sockets and wakes carry only hints; the message and its read position stay in Postgres, so losing a node, a socket or a wake loses no message.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.27.5: duplicate wakes inside 60 s collapse into one, and an extra wake only makes the session read an inbox whose cursor already prevents a second delivery.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.27.7: a slow or failed courier is dropped after its timeout and the 300 s reconciliation (AC-52.27.4) wakes again; where waking does not work the session still gets the message at its next tool round.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.27.3: the wake reaches the session's machine by matching holders.host to the runner's joined machine and travels over PubSub to whichever node holds that runner's socket.

definition_of_done: docs/factory/measurements/idle-session-wake.md exists with a result for minis and for mac-mini, and the runner config's adapter map matches it.
On minis: an interactive session left idle receives the wake text within 30 s of a message_send to its holder id from a session on x1, and its next turn reads the message with inbox.
defaults: Reconciliation interval 300 s; per-holder wake coalescing window 60 s; courier timeout 120 s (owner may change).
Wake text: 'You have unread loopctl inbox messages. Read them with the inbox tool now.'
Only :user and :superadmin keys may subscribe to messages:tenant (fleet_dash).
